turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I've noticed that the situation is escalating quickly. Have you considered the consequences of open conflict between your tenants and my husband's followers?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in a debate with you, Sandip. The situation is serious, and I will not hesitate to take necessary measures to protect my people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, Nikhil, the zamindari estates are not just about power struggles or fear. They are also about the people who depend on us for their livelihoods.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What a delightful new role I'm to play in this drama - the villain, the oppressor, the fearful Zamindar. I'll have you know, Nikhil, that your tenants adore me and would never think of revolting against me.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your words, Sandip. The safety and well-being of my people are of paramount importance, and I will take all necessary measures to ensure their protection.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you're so concerned about your people's well-being, but what about their souls? Don't you think a little fear and uncertainty might be good for their character?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I demand that you take this threat seriously, Sandip, and do not underestimate the capabilities of the local Mussulmans. They have a history of violence, and I will not be responsible for any harm that comes to my people because of your negligence.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what, pray tell, would you do, Nikhil, if the Mussulmans were to attack? Play hero, perhaps, and save the day with your bravery?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, do you truly believe that the people who rely on you for their livelihood would turn against you?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, come now, Nikhil, you're not going to lecture me on responsibility, are you? I'm a zamindar, not some fledgling politician.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in petty banter with you, Sandip. The safety of my people is at stake, and I expect you to take immediate action to address this threat.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what's the world coming to when a rival zamindar starts playing the role of a self-appointed protector of the people? I'm starting to think you're more concerned with looking good in front of your own people than actually doing what's right.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, have you considered the possibility that Nikhil's concerns may be genuine, and that there may be more to this situation than your initial skepticism?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You want me to coddle the villagers' egos, Nikhil? They're not some fragile flowers that need constant reassurance. They're the ones who are supposed to be grateful for my benevolence, not the other way around.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I find it intriguing that you, Nikhil, are so invested in the well-being of the villagers. It suggests a certain level of concern for their welfare, don't you think?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I expect a more thoughtful response from you, Sandip, rather than petty insults. The villagers are not pawns to be used for your own gain, and I will not stand idly by while their safety is threatened.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I would like to clarify what you both mean by 'safety' and 'welfare'. Are you referring to the physical safety of the villagers, or is there something else at play here?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I'm referring to the physical safety of the villagers, Sandip. It's your duty as a landowner to ensure their well-being, and I will not hesitate to take action if I believe you're neglecting your responsibilities.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so serious and solemn. Threats from the Mussulmans? Ha! I've faced down more ferocious beasts at the hunt.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I have noticed that the villagers have been discussing the recent changes in the land distribution. It seems that some of them are concerned about their future prospects.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
